'''Kaarlo Jaakko Juhani Hintikka''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|ɪ|n|t|ɪ|k|ə}}; {{IPA|fi|ˈhintikːɑ|lang}}; 12 January 1929 – 12 August 2015) was a Finnish and American [[philosopher]] and [[logician]]. Hintikka is regarded as the founder of formal [[epistemic logic]] and of [[game semantics]] for logic. He was awarded the [[Rolf Schock Prizes|Rolf Schock Prize]] for philosophy in 2005, and he was chief editor of the philosophical journal ''[[Synthese]]'' 1965–2002.

==Early life and education==
Hintikka was born in [[Helsingin maalaiskunta]] (now Vantaa) outside of Helsinki, Finland on 12 January 1929.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n50036813.html|title=Hintikka, Jaakko, 1929-2015|date=5 August 2025|access-date=31 January 2026|website=Library of Congress}}</ref>

In 1953, he received his doctorate from the [[University of Helsinki]] for a thesis on [[predicate logic]] entitled ''Distributive Normal Forms in the Calculus of Predicates''. He was a student of [[Georg Henrik von Wright]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=JAAKKO HINTIKKA 1929-2015|last=Väänänen|first=Jouko|date=December 2015|journal=The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic|issue=4|volume=21|pages=431–436|jstor=43676827}}</ref> After his doctoral study, he became a [[Junior Fellow]] at [[Harvard University]] (1956–1959).<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Hintikka held professorial appointments at the University of Helsinki (1959–1970), [[Stanford University]] (1965–1982, partially visiting), [[Florida State University]] (1978–1990), and finally [[Boston University]] from 1990 until his death in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Floyd|first1=Juliet|url=http://www.bu.edu/philo/2015/08/13/professor-jaakko-hintikka-1929-2015/|title=Professor Jaakko Hintikka (1929-2015)|date=13 August 2015|website=Boston University Philosophy Department|publisher=Boston University|access-date=2 September 2015}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He was the prolific author or co-author of over 30 books and over 300 scholarly articles. Hintikka contributed to [[mathematical logic]], [[philosophical logic]], the [[philosophy of mathematics]], [[epistemology]], [[Philosophy of language|language theory]], and the [[philosophy of science]]. His works have appeared in over nine languages. In 2005, he won the [[Rolf Schock Prize]] in logic and philosophy "for his pioneering contributions to the logical analysis of modal concepts, in particular the concepts of knowledge and belief".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kva.se/en/news/rolf-schockprisen-2005-2/|title=The Rolf Schock Prizes 2005|date=5 April 2005|access-date=30 January 2026|website=The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

Hintikka served as chief editor of the philosophical journal ''[[Synthese]]'' from 1965 to 2002,<ref name=":0" /> and he was a consultant editor for more than ten journals. He was a vice president of the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]] (1968–1971),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Officers, Council Members, and Executive Committee Members |url=https://aslonline.org/about-the-asl/former-officers-council-members-and-executive-committee-members/ |access-date=7 February 2026 |website=Association for Symbolic Logic}}</ref> a member of the [[American Philosophical Association]] and president of its Pacific division (1975–1976),<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=APA Divisional Presidents and Addresses |url=https://www.apaonline.org/page/presidents |access-date=7 February 2026 |website=American Philosophical Association}}</ref> a member of the governing board of the [[Philosophy of Science Association]] (1970–1974),<ref name=":0" /> president of the [[Florida Philosophical Association]] (1984–1985),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://meta.phil.ufl.edu/host/fpa/index.html?page=officers|title=FPA: Officers|access-date=30 January 2026|website=University of Florida Department of Philosophy}}</ref> the first vice-president of the [[International Federation of Philosophical Societies|Fédération Internationale des Sociétés de Philosophie]] (1993–1998),<ref name=":0" /> a vice-president and president of the [[Institut International de Philosophie]] (1993–1996; 1999–2002),<ref name=":0" /> as well as a president of the [[Charles S. Peirce Society]] (1997)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://peircesociety.org/about/|title=About the Charles S. Peirce Society|access-date=30 January 2026|website=The Charles S. Peirce Society}}</ref>  and the [[International Union of History and Philosophy of Science]].<ref name=":0" />

He was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40104 |title=Gruppe 3: Idéfag |publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] |language=no |access-date=16 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109221405/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40104 |archive-date= 9 January 2015 }}</ref> On May 26, 2000, Hintikka received an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the Faculty of History and Philosophy at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title=Honorary doctorates - Uppsala University, Sweden|website=www.uu.se|access-date=10 April 2018}}</ref>

== Death ==
Hintikka died on 12 August 2015 in [[Porvoo]], Finland.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=JAAKKO HINTIKKA, 1929-2015|last=Floyd|first=Juliet|date=November 2015|journal=Proceedings and Addresses of the American Philosophical Association|volume=89|pages=192–194|jstor=43661514}}</ref>

==Philosophical work==

Early in his career, he devised a [[semantics of modal logic]] essentially analogous to [[Saul Kripke]]'s [[Kripke semantics|frame semantics]], and discovered the now widely taught [[semantic tableau]] independently of [[Evert Willem Beth]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nerode |first=A. |author-link=Anil Nerode |last2=Smullyan |first2=Raymond M. |author-link2=Raymond M. Smullyan |date=March 1962 |title=Reviewed Work: The Foundations of Mathematics, A Study in the Philosophy of Science by Evert W. Beth |journal=The Journal of Symbolic Logic |volume=27 |issue=1 |pages=73–75 |doi=10.2307/2963680 |jstor=2963680}}</ref> Later, he worked mainly on [[game semantics]], and on [[independence-friendly logic]], known for its "[[branching quantifier]]s", which he believed do better justice to our intuitions about [[Quantification (logic)|quantifiers]] than does conventional [[first-order logic]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hintikka |first1=Jaakko |last2=Sandu |first2=Gabriel |year=1996 |title=A Revolution in Logic? |url=https://www.hf.uio.no/ifikk/english/research/publications/journals/njpl/files/vol1no2/revolution.pdf |journal=[[Nordic Journal of Philosophical Logic]]|volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=169–183}}</ref> He did important exegetical work on [[Aristotle]], [[Immanuel Kant]], [[Ludwig Wittgenstein]], and [[Charles Sanders Peirce]]. Hintikka's work can be seen as a continuation of the analytic tendency in philosophy founded by [[Franz Brentano]] and Peirce, advanced by [[Gottlob Frege]] and [[Bertrand Russell]], and continued by [[Rudolf Carnap]], [[Willard Van Orman Quine]], and by Hintikka's teacher [[Georg Henrik von Wright]]. In 1998, for instance, he wrote ''The Principles of Mathematics Revisited'', which takes an exploratory stance comparable to that Russell adopted in his ''[[The Principles of Mathematics]]'' in 1903.

==Selected books==
[[File:Jaakko Hintikka.jpg|thumb|right|Hintikka in 2006.]]
For a bibliography, see Auxier and Hahn (2006).
* 1962. ''Knowledge and Belief – An Introduction to the Logic of the Two Notions'' {{ISBN|1-904987-08-7}}
* 1969. ''Models for Modalities: Selected Essays'' {{ISBN|978-90-277-0598-3}}
* 1973 ''Logic, Language-Games and Information: Kantian Themes in the Philosophy of Logic'' {{ISBN|978-0198243649}}
* 1975. ''The intentions of intentionality and other new models for modalities'' {{ISBN|978-90-277-0634-8}}
* 1976. ''The semantics of questions and the questions of semantics: case studies in the interrelations of logic, semantics, and syntax'' {{ISBN|978-95-1950-535-0}}
* 1989. [https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Logic_of_Epistemology_and_the_Episte.html?id=AOujmpQNGUsC ''The Logic of Epistemology and the Epistemology of Logic''] {{ISBN|0-7923-0040-8}}
* 1996. ''Ludwig Wittgenstein: Half-Truths and One-and-a-Half-Truths'' {{ISBN|0-7923-4091-4}}
* 1996. ''Lingua Universalis vs Calculus Ratiocinator'' {{ISBN|0-7923-4246-1}}
* 1996. [https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Principles_of_Mathematics_Revisited.html?id=k5vDVr8sRSwC ''The Principles of Mathematics Revisited''] {{ISBN|0-521-62498-3}}
* 1998. ''Paradigms for Language Theory and Other Essays'' {{ISBN|0-7923-4780-3}}
* 1998. ''Language, Truth and Logic in Mathematics'' {{ISBN|0-7923-4766-8}}
* 1999. ''Inquiry as Inquiry: A Logic of Scientific Discovery'' {{ISBN|0-7923-5477-X}}
* 2004. ''Analyses of Aristotle'' {{ISBN|1-4020-2040-6}}
* 2007. ''Socratic Epistemology: Explorations of Knowledge-Seeking by Questioning'' {{ISBN|978-0-521-61651-5}}
